# Ice Warriors (game show)

| last_aired   =
}}
Ice Warriors is a British game show which aired on ITV from 24 January to 21 March 1998 and was hosted by Dani Behr. It had a similar format to Gladiators, except that the games were played on an ice rink installed at the Manchester Arena. The show's sponsor was 7 Up.
Although the series won a Bronze Rose for Light Entertainment at the 1998 Rose d'Or Festival, it was not successful with critics and viewers, receiving bad reviews and poor ratings. The show came to an end after one series.
Format
The narrative of the show is explained in the opening title sequence:
After the millennium, a new ice age ravaged the Earth. Entire cities were destroyed, yet deep beneath the frozen ice plains mankind survived. An elite taskforce travelled back through time to prepare it by means of The Tournament. Their task: to ensure the survival of mankind. They were not indestructible, but instructors, not masters, but mentors. They were the Ice Warriors.
Each episode featured two teams of eight athletes and ice skaters, made up four men and four women along with a coach, representing different cities of the UK, competing in what was known as 'The Tournament'. Overseen by the ice master, Shem Jadier (Philip Ferrentinos), the tournament consisted of a series of challenges set on the ice, with each team competing against one other and the Ice Warriors, and were awarded points - or 'credits' as they were known - based on their performance.
The team that earned the most credits won the match and advanced to the final challenge, 'The Polar Pursuit', which was a chase race between four players on the winning team and four of the Ice Warriors. Each of the Ice Warriors that was caught by a player before the finish was worth money to the winning team, the value of which increased during the tournament.
After the six heats, the four teams that earned the most money in 'The Polar Pursuit' returned to contest two semi-finals, the winners of which then faced off against each other in the Grand Final to decide the series champions.
Early episodes also had an entertainment interval of a figure skating performance, but this was dropped mid-way during the series when its running time was reduced.
Ice Warriors
The show attempted to create backstory and lore for the characters drawn from elements of fantasy fiction. Some of those who appeared as the warriors were professional winter athletes.
